phases.message: I'm Odalys, HR at Brackenmere Distribution. Start in Applyrook: read our hiring policy on background reports (every topic), the candidates and the notices already sent.
Veritarn is our background vendor. Read the agency's details and every report it has delivered.

Postwren is my mail and the letter service. Read the inbox, then, by our policy, send each pre-adverse notice that is owed and has not gone, and each final notice that the policy allows today, and send Veritarn any candidate's dispute of a report that it does not already have. Don't reply to anyone. Then tell me, for each notice or dispute, who it went to and why it was due, and what you left alone and why.

policy.text: Today is Friday 9 October 2026. Brackenmere Distribution (118 employees, Harlan Reach, Texas) makes every offer contingent on a background report from Veritarn Screening, and HR sends its own notices. This is Brackenmere's hiring policy, with the federal rule it follows. Topics: authorization, scope, pre-adverse, wait, final, dispute, state.

FCRA 604(b)(2) (15 U.S.C. 1681b): before a report is ordered, the candidate gets a clear, written disclosure in a document that is only the disclosure, and signs an authorization. The ATS shows the date it was signed. A report ordered without one is not used: no rejection rests on it and no notice is sent on it; HR gives it to the compliance lead, Ruth Ellery.

Notices are needed only where the decision to reject rests in whole or in part on the report. A candidate turned down for another reason (a failed skills test, say), one who withdrew, one who was cleared or hired, and one whose report was corrected to clear get no notice of either kind. Brackenmere sends its own notices; the vendor does not send them.

FCRA 604(b)(3)(A): before the rejection, the candidate is sent a copy of the report (by its Veritarn report id) and A Summary of Your Rights Under the Fair Credit Reporting Act (CFPB, 12 CFR 1022 Appendix K), together. Brackenmere sends it within 2 business days of the report arriving, not counting the day it arrives. A notice that went without the copy or the summary is sent again complete, and the wait starts from the new date.

The statute names no number of days; Brackenmere's own policy is 5 full business days after the pre-adverse notice, for the candidate to read the report and answer. Business days are Monday to Friday except company holidays; the day the notice is sent is not counted. The final notice goes on the sixth business day or later. Company holidays this autumn: Monday 12 October (Columbus Day), Wednesday 11 November (Veterans Day), 26 and 27 November, 25 December.

FCRA 615(a) (15 U.S.C. 1681m): after the wait, the final notice names the agency with its address and phone number, says the agency did not make the decision and cannot say why, and tells the candidate of the right to a free copy of the report within 60 days and to dispute it. It goes only where the notice log shows a complete pre-adverse notice with its date, the wait is over, no dispute is open, and the report still shows the record.

A candidate who tells HR that the report is wrong has the right to dispute it with Veritarn (FCRA 611, 1681i). Brackenmere sends Veritarn the candidate's statement, by report id, the day HR reads it, unless the vendor's page already shows the dispute; his final notice waits until Veritarn answers. A report Veritarn has reissued clear ends the matter and nothing more is sent.

Brackenmere hires only at its Harlan Reach, Texas, site, in no city with a fair-chance ordinance, and its counsel finds no state or local rule that adds a step to the notices above. Federal discrimination law is not part of this chore, and no decision here turns on a criminal record's weight.
